issues: Option D uses an IAM SAML provider although Google and Apple sign-in are OIDC-based; the why still holds (custom broker code), but an IAM OIDC provider would be the more natural distractor.

Stem says the company does not want to 'host a second directory in AWS', but the key is an 'AD Connector directory' (AD Connector is created as a directory in AWS Directory Service), so the stem and the key read as contradictory to a careful candidate.
Key itself is documented (sso-ad: AD Connector or Managed AD must reside in the management account).
suggestedFix: Reword the constraint to 'does not want to run AD FS servers or create a new set of user accounts in AWS' (and keep option B as 'Managed AD with re-created accounts').

issues: Near-duplicate of federation-bridge-001 (Organizations accounts, SAML 2.0 IdP, IAM Identity Center); 013 does add the permission-set decision, so keep both but do not let both appear in one mock.

Option A text 'because it is the lowest-scale option' is awkward; the decisive differentiator is IAM Identity Center not supporting Simple AD (sso-ad), which is documented. Simple AD also supports joining Linux domains per ds-what-is, so the LDAP clue alone is not what excludes it; the Identity Center plan does, and it is stated in the stem.
